title: Introduction Mans Purpose And The Declaration Of 2 Abysses

questions.question: Why were people sent to this world, according to the passage?
questions.answer: To know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the first big job of a person?
questions.answer: To learn about Allah and have faith in Him.

questions.question: Besides believing in Allah, what else should a person accept about Him?
questions.answer: That He exists and that He is One.

questions.question: How should a person believe in Allah?
questions.answer: With submission and strong certainty.

questions.question: What kind of life do people naturally want?
questions.answer: A life that lasts forever.

questions.question: Do people have only a few hopes and troubles, or many hopes and troubles?
questions.answer: They have many hopes and many troubles.

questions.question: Which things are most important for a person in the passage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowing Allah, and the ways to reach that.

questions.question: Why are those things so important?
questions.answer: Because they are the base and key for eternal life.

questions.question: How should other goals be seen if they are away from belief and knowing Allah?
questions.answer: They should be seen as small, and sometimes not worth much.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The most important thing in life is faith in Allah, knowing Him, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach is the wisdom of human life in this world?
questions.answer: It is to recognize Allah and worship Him.

questions.question: Who is the Creator mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah, the Creator of everything.

questions.question: What does it mean to recognize the Creator in this passage?
questions.answer: It means to know Allah and believe in Him.

questions.question: What duty comes before other duties in the passage?
questions.answer: Having faith in Allah and knowing Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: A person should believe that Allah is One.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention people’s many troubles?
questions.answer: To show that people need something greater and lasting.

questions.question: What matches people’s many hopes in the passage?
questions.answer: Their many hardships and pains.

questions.question: What gives real value to a person’s life, based on the passage?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and knowing Him.

questions.question: What can help a person reach eternal life?
questions.answer: The means that lead to belief in Allah and knowledge of Him.

questions.question: What can we infer about things like success or stuff if they are without faith?
questions.answer: They are not the most important and may have little value.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person do with the Creator?
questions.answer: Know Him, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: Is the passage about only believing with words, or also with obedience and certainty?
questions.answer: Also with obedience and certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say people deeply want?
questions.answer: To live forever.

questions.question: Why might ordinary things not be enough for a person?
questions.answer: Because people want lasting life and have many deep needs.

questions.question: What two special treasures are named for a person?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: What are these treasures connected to?
questions.answer: Eternal life.

questions.question: If something does not help with faith or knowing Allah, how should it be judged?
questions.answer: As low in worth, or sometimes worthless.

questions.question: What feeling should a believer have in faith, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Strong certainty.

questions.question: What lesson should a 2nd-grade student take from this passage?
questions.answer: The biggest goal is to know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the purpose of being sent into the world?
questions.answer: To know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is one wise reason for human life mentioned here?
questions.answer: So people can recognize their Creator.

questions.question: Does the passage describe Allah as creator of some things or all things?
questions.answer: All things.

questions.question: What belief about Allah must a person hold?
questions.answer: That Allah is real and that He is One.

questions.question: What should go together with faith: doubt or firm certainty?
questions.answer: Firm certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human hopes?
questions.answer: They are very many.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human sufferings?
questions.answer: They are also very many.

questions.question: Why does the passage make belief sound more important than other things?
questions.answer: Because belief and knowing Allah lead to everlasting life.

questions.question: How are other things described when compared with faith in Allah?
questions.answer: They are described as lesser, and sometimes of no real worth.

questions.question: What is one good summary sentence for the passage?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah and worshipping Him is the greatest purpose of life.

questions.question: Who should people come to know in this world?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What should people do after knowing Allah?
questions.answer: Believe in Him and worship Him.

questions.question: What is called the basic duty of a person?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah and having faith in Him.

questions.question: What truth about Allah must be accepted?
questions.answer: That He exists and that He is One.

questions.question: How complete should a person’s faith be?
questions.answer: It should be full of submission and certainty.

questions.question: What kind of future do people naturally long for?
questions.answer: One that never ends.

questions.question: Why are many people not satisfied with small things?
questions.answer: Because they have huge hopes and many hardships.

questions.question: What things are said to be the foundation for eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the ways to gain them.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about things that are apart from these?
questions.answer: They are not very important and may even be worthless.

questions.question: What matters most in a person’s life, based on this passage?
questions.answer: Faith, knowing Allah, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: According to the passage, why did Allah send people to this world?
questions.answer: So they can know Him, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say is built into human life by wisdom?
questions.answer: A purpose to recognize the Creator.

questions.question: What is the very first responsibility of a human being here?
questions.answer: To know Allah and believe in Him.

questions.question: What important belief about Allah is included in that responsibility?
questions.answer: Believing that Allah is One.

questions.question: What attitude should a person have toward Allah’s truth?
questions.answer: Humble acceptance and sure faith.

questions.question: What are two things people carry in their hearts by nature?
questions.answer: Big hopes and a wish to keep living.

questions.question: What else do people face in life besides hopes?
questions.answer: Many pains and troubles.

questions.question: Why does the passage place belief in Allah above everything else?
questions.answer: Because it opens the way to eternal life.

questions.question: What can we understand about worldly things from this passage?
questions.answer: They are not the highest good if they are without faith.

questions.question: If a child asked for the central message of the passage, what would you say?
questions.answer: Our greatest purpose is to know Allah, trust Him, and worship Him.
